Kh. Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Pathan Shafiqur Rahman ------ For the Respondents 1 to 3.

Vs.

full_judgment:
This appeal is at the instance of a tenant against a concurrent judgment decreeing a suit for ejectment and recovery of arrear rent. 

 2. The facts out of which the present appeal has arisen may be stated as follows: According to the plffs. Case the father of the defendants was a monthly tenant under the plffs. In the suit premises according to the English calendar month at a monthly rent of Rs.40/- and after the death of their father the defendants became the monthly tenants under the plffs. The defendants were habitual defaulters and they defaulted in making payment of rent from February, 1958 to September, 1960. A suit was brought by the plaintiffs being Title Suit No. 229 of 1960 for ejectment as well as for recovery of arrear rent amounting to Rs. 1,280/-. This suit was decreed on 17-5-61 for arrears of rent only and in pursuance of the direction contained in the said decree the defendants deposited a sum of Rs. 1,745/45 paisa towards the arrear rents as mentioned above and costs of the suit. This amount was withdrawn by the plaintiffs but in the appeal, which was preferred against the said decree, the decree was set aside and the case was sent back to the trial court on remand for rehearing. After rehearing the suit was again decree with costs on 28-12-61 for arrears of rent only, amounting to Rs. 1,280/- but the prayer for ejectment was rejected. It appears that before the Title Suit No. 229 of 1980 had been instituted, as House Rent Control Case being House Rent Control Case No. 239 of 1959 was started by the defendants for depositing the rent and sum of Rs. 720/- was deposited amount of Rs. 40/- was deposited on 10-9-59 [vide Exts. E and E(1)]. Before the present suit had been instituted on 9-10-63, the defendants by a letter dated 16-2-62 intimated the plaintiff that a sum of Rs 760/- had been in deposit in House Rent Control Case No. 239 of 1959 which might be withdrawn by the plaintiffs towards the house rent upto April, 1962. The rent of May, 1962 was thereafter sent by Money Order by the defendants on 11-5-1962 and this appears to have been refused by the plaintiffs on 20-6-62. Thereafter on 18-7-1962 the House Rent Control Case No. 365(a)/62 [vide Ext. D(3)] was started for depositing arrear rents but no rent was deposited in the said House Rent Control Case. Then on 9-10-63 the present suit has been filed for ejectment of the tenants on the ground that the defendants are habitual defaulters and also that the plaintiffs bonafide require the premises for their own use and occupation. It is also asserted in the plaint that a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act has been served upon the defendants terminating their tenancy. There is also a prayer for recovery of arrear rents for the period from October, 1960 to September, 1963 amounting to a sum of Rs. 1,440/-. It is also asserted in the plaint that a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, has been served upon the defendants terminating their tenancy. There is also a prayer for recovery of arrear rents for the period from October, 1960 to September, 1963 amounting to a sum of Rs. 1,440/-. The suit was contested by the defendants by filing a written statement in which the main allegations of the plaintiffs have been denied. It has been asserted in the said written statement that the defendants are not defaulters as they repeated the plaintiffs to withdraw the amount in the House Rent Control Case and thereafter the rent for the month of May, 1962 was sent by Money Order which being refused the House Rent Control Case No. 365 of 1962 has been started for permission to deposit the rent and that the said case is still pending. It has also been stated that the plaintiffs do not require the house bonafide for their own use and occupation. 

 5. Mr. Ahmed Subhan submits that the defendants have been trying to make regular payment of rent to the plaintiffs but because of the plaintiffs, refusal to accept payment of rent from them they had to start a House Rent Control Case I959 in which they deposited an amount of Rs 760/- then made a payment of Rs 1,745/- and odd including an amount of Rs 1,280/- towards the rent of the disputed premises in pursuance of a decree of the Court and then again they had to start another House Rent Control Case in 1962 before the institution of the present suit on account of the refusal of the plaintiffs to accept rent from them and in view of the fact that no permision was granted by the House Rent Controller to deposit the amount, nothing could be deposited in the said case before the decree was passed. The learned  advocate contends that in view of the aforesaid facts it cannot be said that the defendants are defaulters within the meaning of House Rent Control Ordinance. 

 6. I do not think that the learned Advocate is correct in his contention. The provisions of House Rent Control Ordinance, as have been interepted in a number of judicial decisions of the Dacca High Court, clearly lay down that the denfandants are not entitled to the benefit of the said Ordinance unless they pay the rent due by him in respect of such premises to the full extent winthin the time fixed in the contract or within 15 day of the month next following for which the rent is payable. In a case when the landlord refuses to accept the rent, the tenant has to deposit such rent or any subsequent rent in respect of the premises in accordance with the provisions laid down in section 19 of the Ordinance. Section 19 of the Ordinance clearly provides that when the landlord refused to accept any rent remitted by the Postal Money Order by the tenant in respect of the premises the tenant may deposit such rent within a fortnight from the day on which the rent remitted is returned to the tenant by the Postal authority. It has been laid down in the case of Md. Aktar Vs. Md Abdus Saddique reported in 8 D L R. 272 that the tenant is to tender the arrear rent to the Rent Controller and the Rent Controller shall have to accept the said rent without going in to the question of correctness of the statements made by the tenant in his application for deposit of rent. The time for deposit of such rent being of essence as will appear from sub-section (5) of section 18; any loss of time for the purpose of ascertainment of certain facts by the Rent Controller does not appear to be contemplated by the said provisions. Therefore, in my opinion, failure to deposit the amount of rent on the alleged ground that the necessary permission of the House Rent Controller has not been accorded for such deposit will not protect the tenant from being a defaulter within the meaning of sub-section (5) of section 18 of the Ordinance. The case of Md. Aktar Vs. Md. Abdus Saddique reported in 8 DLR 272 as well as the case of Haji Afizuddin Ahmed Vs. A K M Ashraf Ali reported in P.L.D. 1968 Dacca 942 may be referred to in support of this view. In this connection the case of Abdul Hafiz Abdul Nabi Vs. M. Daud Ali reported in P.L.D 1961 Dacca 34 where Rahman, J. (as he then was) has observed that the provisions of Rent Control Ordinance shall have to be strictly construed as it purports to take away some of the rights of the persons which they otherwise enjoy under the ordinary law of the country and also the case of Mullah Mahbub Ali & ors. Vs. Janab Ali & another reported in 8 D.L.R. 448 as well as the case of Ananda Sundari Karmakar Vs. Dr. Mozammel Huq reported in 12 D.L R. 720 where it has been held that the material time to consider whether there has been any default in the payment of rent is the date on which the decree in the suit comes to be passed by the Court may be referred to. 

 7. In this case the defendants cannot be taken to be defaulters in respect of the rent unto September, 1960 as will appear from the decree passed in Title Suit No. 229 of 1960. But after September, 1960 it does not appear there was any valid tender of rent. It is contended by the learned Advocate for the appellants that an amount of Rs. 760/- having been in deposit in House Rent Control Case. No. 229 of 1959 to the credit of the plaintiffs, it was up-to the plaintiffs to withdraw the said amount. Both the Courts below have taken the view that it was not until 16-2-62 that the plaintiffs were informed that the amount in deposit in the said House Rent Control Case could be withdrawn for the purpose of satisfying their claim of rent from October, 1960 to April, 1962. It is not known whether the deposit made in the said case which was in respect of the rent due prior to the institution of the Title Suit No. 229 of 1960 was validly made. However, since this money was deposited on account of some other purpose and there is no evidence on record to show that the plaintiffs were requested to withdraw the money at any time before 166.62, I do not think that the Courts below were wrong in taking the view that the said deposit could not be taken to be valid tender for the payment of rent for the period October, 1960 to April, 1962. Secondly front Ext. 6 it appears that the money order for the rent of May, 1962 was refused on 20.6.62 but the House Rent Control Case was not started before 18-7-62 and it is admitted that no deposit was made in the said House Rent Control Case before the decree was passed. I do not therefore; think that in view of the aforesaid facts it can be held that he defendants paid up the rent due within the time as required under the law.
